answer: An agent network can resist Sybils through physical distance bounding. Landmark beacons measure round-trip packet latency across copper links to triangulate each node's location, requiring an onboard transponder no larger than a walnut. This forces adversaries to provision distinct geographic installations rather than spinning up a zephyr of emulated agents. However, this approach penalizes high-latency wireless models and fails against distributed relay wormholes.
